chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who freezes (withholds distribution of) one-third of the deceased's estate due to the execution of a will, and he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Execute one-third and do not freeze it.'
Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ubaydi narrated, saying: Ahmad ibn Hamzah wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him):
A debt was frozen, then its owner died, and he had a debt that his wealth could not cover, so he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'His frozen assets are sold to pay the debt.'

key_terms.وَقْفُهُ: his frozen assets / his withheld portion

ai.seo_question: How is one-third of an estate handled if the deceased has debts that exceed their total wealth?
ai.summary: These narrations from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarify the procedural priority of executing the one-third bequest (al-thuluth) over withholding it, ensuring the testator's wishes are fulfilled promptly. Furthermore, they establish that if the estate is insufficient to cover debts, the frozen assets designated for bequests are liquidated to settle creditors, highlighting the balance between the deceased's intent and financial obligations in Shia jurisprudence. This reflects the practical application of inheritance law where debt settlement and bequest execution are integrated rather than strictly sequential in cases of insolvency.
